clue.text: Stony Rocker gets 2 in ad- advance

indicators.note: the cross-referenced letter is placed within the word for a loan of money

parts.note: an advance of money is a loan
2 refers to the answer of 2-down, a thousand pounds, for which G is the usual short form

explanation.surface: A rock musician with a heart of stone collects a fee up front.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'Rocker' is not a musician but a rocking stone: in Cornwall a balanced boulder that rocks at a touch is called by this name.
explanation.definitionFit: A logan stone is a large boulder so balanced that it rocks when pushed, hence a stony rocker.

clue.text: Like Banquo's ghost he's no early arrival

definitions.text: Like Banquo's ghost he's no early arrival

parts.words: Like Banquo's ghost he's no early arrival
parts.note: in Macbeth the murdered Banquo's ghost turns up at the banquet after everyone has sat down, someone arriving behind time

explanation.surface: Shakespeare's murdered Banquo, returning as a ghost, is no punctual guest.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who turns up after the start is a tardy arrival, as Banquo's ghost is at Macbeth's feast.

clue.text: States money placed by 10 at the races

definitions.meaning: in the United States a thousand dollars is called by this slang word
put beside the answer to 10-across it makes the spectators' stand at a racecourse

explanation.surface: American cash bet by a punter at the racecourse.
explanation.walkthrough: 10 is the answer to 10-across, STAND; set beside it, this word makes GRANDSTAND, the main spectator stand at a racecourse.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for a thousand dollars, and the first part of the compound naming the main stand at a racecourse.

clue.text: Emperor's refusal to hold a rod

indicators.note: the refusal word grips the other pieces inside it, as a hand holds a rod

parts.note: non is French for no, a refusal
a pole is a rod

explanation.surface: An emperor declines to carry a staff of office.
explanation.definitionFit: Bonaparte crowned himself ruler of the French Empire in 1804.

clue.text: Authorized monopoly?

parts.note: an author is granted the sole legal right to reproduce a work, a monopoly given to authors

explanation.surface: A government-sanctioned exclusive trading privilege.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Authorized' reads as officially permitted, but it also means given to an author.
explanation.definitionFit: The legal right protecting a writer's work gives its author exclusive control over reproduction.

clue.text: As such, 3 was gold

parts.note: 3 is the answer to 3-down; the French twenty-franc gold piece bore that emperor's name

explanation.surface: In this form, the emperor was made of precious metal.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a gilded statue of the emperor, but a napoleon was a French gold piece of money.
explanation.definitionFit: A napoleon was a gold twenty-franc piece of currency, so as money it was gold.

clue.text: Coo! Twins!

parts.note: the exclamation of surprise also suggests the cooing of doves; twins of one boy and one girl are called by a bird-based name, as a dove's brood is usually one of each sex

explanation.surface: Someone's astonished cry at the arrival of twins.
explanation.definitionFit: Twins of opposite sexes, named after a dove's usual clutch of two eggs, male and female.

clue.text: A green shade serves retrospectively in this

indicators.note: looking back means the letters are taken from right to left
the letters sit within the two clue words that follow green

explanation.surface: A particular hue of green does the job in this colour scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' marks letters within 'shade serves' (ADESER), and 'retrospectively' says read them backwards. 'this' is a link pointing to the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Reseda, named after the mignonette plant, is a greyish-green colour.

clue.text: Republic faced a U-turn during the festivity

indicators.note: the reversed pieces come in the middle of the festivity word

parts.note: a gala is a festivity

indicators.note: the U-turn of the surface means the pieces before it are turned round

parts.note: to have faced someone is to have met them
the letter as printed in U-turn

explanation.surface: A republic did an about-face in the middle of the celebrations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'faced' is the past tense, to have met someone; the 'U-turn' of the surface supplies both the letter U and the signal 'turn', which reverses everything before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Guatemala is a Central American country with a republican constitution.

clue.text: Regular turns by these at coastal resorts

definitions.text: Regular turns by these at coastal resorts

parts.words: Regular turns by these at coastal resorts
parts.note: the sea comes in and goes out twice a day at the shore, a turn like a variety act at a seaside show

explanation.surface: Seaside entertainers performing their acts at holiday towns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns' suggests stage acts at seaside resorts, but it is the sea turning, in and out, regularly.
explanation.definitionFit: The sea's rise and fall happens on a regular cycle, turning at high and low water.

clue.text: Nag, spirit broken, plodding on

indicators.note: something broken is in pieces, so these letters are reassembled in a new order

explanation.surface: A horse, its spirit crushed, trudges onward.
explanation.definitionFit: To traipse is to walk wearily, so the -ing form is trudging along.

clue.text: Bear tu get up on hind feet

definitions.meaning: to bear something is to tolerate it
to rise upright, as an animal rearing does

explanation.surface: A bear rears up on its back legs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bear' reads as the animal, which does indeed rear up, but it is the verb, to tolerate.
explanation.definitionFit: Tolerate, and also rise to an upright position.

clue.text: To pumper a child shouldn't make him hard-boiled

definitions.text: a child shouldn't make him hard-boiled
definitions.meaning: eggs cooked this way are simmered gently below boiling, so they never come out hard

explanation.surface: Indulging a child should not make him a tough cynic.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading turns on eggs: to cook an egg gently in water just below boiling point.
explanation.definitionFit: To spoil someone with excessive care, and to cook eggs gently below the boil.

clue.text: For this, proverbially, we have no information

definitions.text: For this, proverbially, we have no information

parts.words: For this, proverbially, we have no information
parts.note: the proverb says that hearing nothing is itself a welcome report

explanation.surface: A saying about something of which we know nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb is 'No news is good news'.
explanation.definitionFit: A welcome report, which the proverb equates with hearing nothing at all.

clue.text: Far from 19 sign of hesitancy by a habitue

parts.note: 19 refers to the answer of 19-across, uncommon; far from uncommon is happening often
er is the sound of someone hesitating

explanation.surface: A regular who is anything but rare, hesitating as he speaks.
explanation.definitionFit: A habitué is a regular visitor to a place, one who goes there often.

clue.text: Quietly play round with diagram of apparatus to get the 4 ac?

parts.note: to mime is to act without words, playing silently
the round shape of the letter O
a graph is a diagram

explanation.surface: Acting out a silent play around a diagram of a machine.
explanation.walkthrough: 4 ac is 4-across, COPYRIGHT; the machine makes copies, the playful question being whether it gets you the right to them.
explanation.definitionFit: A stencil duplicator, an early office copying machine.

clue.text: Understand sun-god enters war-god's ' celebration

indicators.note: the first two pieces go inside the name of the war-god

parts.note: Mars is the Roman god of war
to dig is slang for to understand
Ra is the Egyptian sun-god

explanation.surface: A sun-god joins a war-god's party.
explanation.walkthrough: MARDI GRAS is Shrove Tuesday, the carnival before Lent.
explanation.definitionFit: Shrove Tuesday's carnival, a festival before the Lenten fast begins.

clue.text: Fish deep in the sound

definitions.meaning: a sea or freshwater perch-like fish
low in pitch, the lowest part in music

explanation.surface: A fish living deep down in a sea inlet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' looks like a stretch of sea where the fish swims, but it means musical sound.
explanation.definitionFit: A perch-like fish, and the lowest musical register.

clue.text: Associated with crooks, their purse is growing

definitions.text: Associated with crooks, their purse is growing

parts.words: Associated with crooks, their purse is growing
parts.note: those who herd sheep carry hooked staffs, and a common weed with purse-shaped pods bears their name

explanation.surface: People linked with criminals whose takings keep rising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crooks' and 'purse' suggest criminals getting rich, but the crook is a hooked staff and shepherd's purse is a wild plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheep-keepers carry crooks, and shepherd's purse is a common weed that grows wild.

clue.text: Henry Ford as tram-driver ?

parts.note: the car maker was a man of motor cars; the driver of a tram is called by the same compound

explanation.surface: Imagining the famous carmaker at the controls of a tram.
explanation.walkthrough: Henry Ford founded the Ford Motor Company; the word also names someone who drives an electric tram or train.
explanation.definitionFit: The driver of a tram or electric train, and a fair description of a car manufacturer.

clue.text: Is this steak order so uncommon?

definitions.meaning: how a diner asks for steak cooked lightly, red inside

explanation.surface: A diner wonders whether ordering steak this way is unusual.
explanation.definitionFit: Lightly cooked meat, and seldom met.

clue.text: Mislead a quiet cove

indicators.note: the letters are led astray into a new order, as a misled person goes the wrong way

explanation.surface: Deceiving some silent chap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mislead' does double service: it rearranges A QUIET COVE, and the whole clue describes speaking ambiguously to deceive someone. 'cove' is old British slang for a man.
explanation.definitionFit: To speak ambiguously so as to deceive, which misleads the listener.

clue.text: Bird sound from a catfish?

definitions.meaning: a fish that was a cat of the ocean would make a feline cry

explanation.surface: Wondering what noise a catfish makes.
explanation.walkthrough: The pun reads a catfish as a sea cat, whose cry would be a mew; the seamew is the common gull.
explanation.definitionFit: The common gull, and a sea cat's cry.

clue.text: Given the fuller biblical treatment

parts.note: a fuller bleached cloth; Mark 9:3 says Christ's garments shone as no fuller on earth could make them

explanation.surface: Treated at greater length, the way the Bible would.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fuller' looks like 'more complete', but a fuller was a tradesman who cleaned and bleached cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: Bleached, made pale, as a fuller treats cloth.

clue.text: Refuse a vital statistic, say

indicators.note: this asks for a word pronounced the same as the measurement

parts.note: the waist is one of the three vital statistics, bust, waist and hips

explanation.surface: Declining to reveal one's measurements.
explanation.definitionFit: Rubbish, the noun sense of refuse, discarded material.

clue.text: But no such back scat on a Jumbo jet

definitions.text: But no such back scat on a Jumbo jet

parts.words: But no such back scat on a Jumbo jet
parts.note: a seat for riding on the back of an elephant, Jumbo being a famous elephant, unlike the seats of a jumbo airliner

explanation.surface: A jumbo airliner has no seat of this kind at the rear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jumbo jet' suggests a Boeing 747, but Jumbo was a famous elephant; this seat sits on an elephant's back.
explanation.definitionFit: A canopied seat carried on an elephant's back.

clue.text: Churned-up mud at the baseline

indicators.note: churned material is stirred round, so these letters are mixed into a new order

explanation.surface: Mud is stirred up at the back line of a tennis court.
explanation.definitionFit: A reference point or level from which measurements are taken.

clue.text: Sad expression of a girl losing point

indicators.note: the girl word drops a letter

parts.note: a lass is a girl
S, south, is a compass point

explanation.surface: A girl looks sad after losing a point in a game.
explanation.definitionFit: An exclamation of grief or regret.

clue.text: Be off! To wit, drive home!

parts.note: sc. is short for scilicet, Latin for namely
to ram something in is to drive it home

explanation.surface: Telling someone to leave and head home.
explanation.definitionFit: Go away! A command to leave at once.

clue.text: It records readings by radio -or TV?

definitions.text: It records readings by radio -or TV?

parts.words: It records readings by radio -or TV?
parts.note: an instrument transmitting measurements remotely, playfully read as a television measurer

explanation.surface: A device that tracks what people listen to or watch.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer splits as TELE + METER, a television meter, though it is an instrument sending data by radio.
explanation.definitionFit: An instrument that measures remotely and transmits its data by radio.

clue.text: The way the world gues round

definitions.text: The way the world gues round

parts.words: The way the world gues round
parts.note: the earth spins from west towards the sunrise

explanation.surface: How things go in life generally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The way the world goes' sounds like a resigned saying, but it is literally the direction of the earth's spin.
explanation.definitionFit: The earth rotates toward the sunrise, from west to the other side.

clue.text: Juliet's roses smelling as sweet by other means?

definitions.text: Juliet's roses smelling as sweet by other means?

parts.words: Juliet's roses smelling as sweet by other means?
parts.note: Juliet says a rose by any other label would smell as sweet

explanation.surface: Romeo and Juliet's famous line about roses.
explanation.walkthrough: In Shakespeare, Juliet says 'that which we call a rose by any other name would smell as sweet'.
explanation.definitionFit: Words people call things by, which Juliet says do not alter a rose's scent.
